### Observed differences

- In the later window, A36 is less frequent: mean occurrences per trace drop from 0.40 to 0.18, and the share of traces containing it from about 25% to 13%. [OCC001]
- The main successors of A19 and A20 change from A23 (about 97% and 95% of outgoing transitions) to A28 (about 95% and 96%). [DIR001, DIR002]
- The main successors of A21 and A22 change from A28 (about 47% and 50%) to A23 (about 50% and 44%); A27's successors change from A21/A22 to A20/A19. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- A38's successors change from A19/A20 (about 45%/40%) to A22/A21 (about 44%/42%). [DIR007]
- Positions shift: A19 and A20 move later (mean position from about 0.37 to 0.66–0.67), while A21 and A22 move earlier (from about 0.66 to 0.38). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]
- Order relations reverse: before, A19/A20 preceded A21/A22/A23/A27 in about half of cases; after, A21/A22/A23/A27 preceded A19/A20 in about half. Within that, A23/A27 preceded A21/A22 in about 98% of cases before, and A21/A22 preceded A23/A27 in about 98% after. [REL001–REL012]
- Lag evidence shows A28 now immediately follows A20 (lag 1 in about 97% of after cases, versus lag 5 before, though before support is only one trace), and A27 now immediately precedes A20 (lag 1 in about 98% after, versus before support of two traces). [LAG001, LAG004]
- A38's relation to A19/A20 changes from immediate predecessor (lag 1 in about 83–85% before) to lag 2/3 after, consistent with A19/A20 moving later. [LAG015, LAG016]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural reordering rather than chance variation: the number of flagged items is many times larger than the 0.67 expected if nothing changed. The positional, relational, and successor indicators agree that A19 and A20 moved from an early position before A21/A22/A23/A27 to a later position after them, while A21 and A22 moved earlier; A28 became the successor of A19/A20 instead of A23, and A36 became less frequent. The main limitation is that some lag items rest on very few traces (e.g., LAG001 before support is 1), but the core reordering is supported by high-support relational and positional items. A competing explanation based solely on sampling differences in variant frequencies is unlikely given the consistency of the order reversals, though the underlying business reason is not identified. [OCC001, DIR001–DIR007, POS001–POS006, REL001–REL012, LAG001, LAG004, LAG015, LAG016]

Support level: Supported hypothesis
